bmtxlP%swvG4Kc0K6bbH.text:
This is a clever boolean trick that lets me create complex conditionals and lower block counts. Basically, it means that if the costume name contains the semicolon but isn't just a semicolon, this will return true. The proper name for a conditional like this is XOR, which is basically like someone saying, “you can take ONE and ONE only”. AKA, it'll only return true if one value is true and the other is false. So, you might be thinking, “What if the second conditional was true and not the first? Wouldn't that still work?” Well, remember that a value can't equal something but not contain it! The opposite to this is XNOR, which is basically this, but without the not block. This is basically, “all or nothing”. AKA, both have to be either true or false—their values can't be different. 

This is a rather useful tip I think was worth sharing. If you're an experienced game maker like me, this will most likely be a game-changer! Thanks for reading!
